newsitem.title: INDIA: IMF SAYS INDIA DEFICIT TARGET DIFFICULT-CHIDAMBARA.
newsitem.headline: IMF SAYS INDIA DEFICIT TARGET DIFFICULT-CHIDAMBARA.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) believes it will be difficult for India to reduce its fiscal deficit as a proportion of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997/98, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Friday.
India hopes to slash its fiscal deficit to 4.5 percent of GDP in 1997/98 from 5.0 percent a year earlier.

"The IMF, after consultations with India in July 1997 has noted that while India's overall economic performance had remained broadly favourable, the targeted reduction of fiscal deficit in 1997/98 might be difficult to achieve if the anticipated revenue receipts did not materialise," Chidambaram told parliament.
"Government will endeavour to contain the fiscal deficit by increasing receipts and restricting expenditure," Chidambaram added.
In a separate statement, junior Finance Minister Satpal Maharaj said the IMF Board recognised India's potential.

"They felt that the recent slowdown in industrial production and exports was, to a considerable extent, a consequence of the partial nature of the reforms which had contributed to infrastructure bottlenecks and continuing constraints in the financial sector," Maharaj said.
The Commerce Ministry said on Friday that exports fell by 0.95 percent to $8.13 billion in the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) from $8.21 billion a year earlier.
Exports in June rose by just 2.53 percent to $2.66 billion from $2.59 billion in June 1996.
